The explosion, one of the largest non-nuclear blasts in history, created a massive crater measuring 1,200 meters across and 120 meters deep.

image.caption: Aerial photograph of the crater left by the RAF Fauld explosion.
image.credit: Royal Air Force — https://historicengland.org.uk/images-books/archive/collections/aerial-photos/record/raf_106g_la_69_po_0018
image.date_qualification: Photographed 4 December 1944; aftermath image, not a photograph of the explosion itself.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: RAF Fauld explosion

events.enhanced_description: On November 29, 1944, the American submarine USS Archerfish successfully sank the Japanese aircraft carrier Shinano, which was the largest carrier ever built at that time. This event marked a significant moment in naval warfare, as it remained the largest ship sunk by a submarine throughout the twentieth century.
events.name: Sinking of USS Archerfish

events.enhanced_description: On December 1, 1944, Edward Stettinius, Jr. was appointed as the last United States Secretary of State under President Franklin D. Roosevelt, succeeding Cordell Hull. His tenure was marked by significant events as the U.S. navigated the final stages of World War II.
events.name: Edward Stettinius, Jr. becomes Secretary of State

events.enhanced_description: On December 3, 1944, an event involving the Home Guard in the United Kingdom occurred, although specific details are not well-documented. The Home Guard played a crucial role in the defense of Britain during World War II, particularly in the face of potential invasion.
events.name: Home Guard event

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1944, the Convention on International Civil Aviation was signed in Chicago, leading to the establishment of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). This agreement aimed to promote safe and orderly development of international civil aviation.
events.name: Convention on International Civil Aviation signed

events.enhanced_description: On December 10, 1944, renowned Italian conductor Arturo Toscanini led a concert performance of the first half of Beethoven's Fidelio on NBC Radio, featuring soprano Rose Bampton. This performance was significant for its political message against tyranny, intended as a tribute to the oppressed German people during World War II.
events.name: Arturo Toscanini conducts Fidelio

events.enhanced_description: On December 12, 1944, British units attempted to capture the Italian hilltop town of Tossignano but were repulsed. This engagement was part of the broader military operations in Italy during World War II, reflecting the challenges faced by Allied forces.
events.name: British units repulsed at Tossignano

events.enhanced_description: On December 13, 1944, during World War II, U.S., Australian, and Philippine Commonwealth troops landed on Mindoro Island in the Philippines as part of a strategic operation to secure the area and prepare for further advances against Japanese forces.
events.name: Battle of Mindoro

events.enhanced_description: On December 14, 1944, the Soviet government initiated a campaign to change Turkish place names to Russian in the Crimea. This action was part of broader efforts to assert Soviet control and influence in the region following World War II.
events.name: Soviet government changes place names in Crimea

events.enhanced_description: On December 15, 1944, a U.S. Army Air Forces utility aircraft carrying bandleader Major Glenn Miller disappeared in heavy fog over the English Channel while en route to Paris. Miller's disappearance remains one of the enduring mysteries of World War II.
events.name: Glenn Miller's aircraft disappears

events.enhanced_description: On December 18, 1944, General Douglas MacArthur was promoted to the rank of Five-Star General, becoming the second individual in U.S. history to hold this prestigious title. This promotion recognized his significant contributions to the Allied war effort in the Pacific during World War II.
events.name: Douglas MacArthur becomes Five-Star General

events.enhanced_description: Le Monde, one of France's most prominent daily newspapers, began publication on December 19, 1944, during a time of significant political and social change in post-World War II France. The newspaper has since played a crucial role in French journalism and public discourse.
events.name: Le Monde begins publication

events.enhanced_description: On December 20, 1944, the United States Women Airforce Service Pilots (WASP) were officially disbanded after serving crucial roles in ferrying aircraft and training male pilots during World War II. Their contributions were significant yet often overlooked in the history of women's participation in the military.

image.caption: Elizabeth L. Remba Gardner, a WASP pilot, looks around before taking off at Harlingen Army Air Field, Texas.
image.credit: US Department of the Air Force. — https://research.archives.gov/description/542191
image.date_qualification: Circa 1943; the image is not a photograph of the December 20, 1944 disbandment.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Disbandment of the Women Airforce Service Pilots

events.enhanced_description: On December 22, 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge, Brigadier General Anthony C. McAuliffe famously responded 'Nuts!' to a German ultimatum demanding the surrender of American forces in Bastogne. This defiant reply became a symbol of American resolve during World War II.
events.name: McAuliffe's 'Nuts!' response

events.enhanced_description: On December 24, 1944, the troopship SS Léopoldville was sunk in the English Channel by the German submarine U-486, resulting in the tragic loss of approximately 763 soldiers from the U.S. 66th Infantry Division, who were en route to the Battle of the Bulge.
events.name: Sinking of SS Léopoldville

events.enhanced_description: On December 24, 1944, a race riot broke out in Agana, Guam, between white and black United States Marines. This incident highlighted the racial tensions present in the military during World War II and the complexities of race relations in the United States.
events.name: Agana race riot

events.enhanced_description: On December 26, 1944, American troops successfully repulsed German forces attempting to capture Bastogne during the Battle of the Bulge. This strategic victory was crucial in preventing the encirclement of Allied forces and contributed to the eventual Allied success in the campaign.

image.caption: U.S. Army Signal Corps photograph of 101st Airborne troops watching C-47s drop supplies near Bastogne.
image.credit: U.S. Army Signal Corps photographer — http://olive-drab.com/gallery/category_004.php
image.date_qualification: Taken in Bastogne on 26 December 1944, during the siege’s relief; this depicts an aerial resupply, not the repulse of German forces itself.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: American troops repulse German forces at Bastogne

events.enhanced_description: On December 30, 1944, King George II of Greece declared a regency, leaving his throne vacant amidst the political turmoil following World War II. This decision was part of the broader struggle between royalists and communists that would lead to the Greek Civil War.
events.name: King George II of Greece declares a regency

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Leyte, which concluded on December 31, 1944, resulted in a significant victory for Filipino and Allied forces against the Imperial Japanese Army. This battle was pivotal in the liberation of the Philippines during World War II.
events.name: Battle of Leyte

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Germany initiated Operation Bodenplatte, a major Luftwaffe offensive aimed at crippling Allied air forces in the Low Countries. This operation was part of a broader strategy to regain air superiority as the war neared its conclusion.
events.name: Operation Bodenplatte

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, the Chenogne massacre occurred when German prisoners were allegedly killed by American forces near the village of Chenogne, Belgium. This incident raised significant ethical questions regarding wartime conduct.
events.name: Chenogne massacre

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, the Soviet Union occupied Warsaw, Poland, marking a significant moment in the liberation of the city from Nazi control. This occupation would lead to the establishment of a communist government in Poland.
events.name: Occupation of Warsaw

events.enhanced_description: During the Siege of Budapest in early 1945, Swedish diplomat Raoul Wallenberg, who had saved thousands of Jews from the Holocaust, was taken into custody by a Soviet patrol. He was never seen publicly again, raising questions about his fate.
events.name: Raoul Wallenberg's detention

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Germany began the evacuation of East Prussia as Soviet forces advanced. This evacuation was part of the larger collapse of German military positions in the region.
events.name: Evacuation of East Prussia

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Hungary agreed to an armistice with the Allies, signaling a shift in the balance of power in Central Europe as World War II drew to a close.
events.name: Hungary's armistice with the Allies

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Grand Admiral Karl Dönitz ordered Operation Hannibal, a mass evacuation of German troops and civilians from the Courland Pocket, East Prussia, and the Polish Corridor. This operation aimed to save an estimated 800,000-900,000 civilians and 350,000 soldiers from advancing Soviet forces.
events.name: Operation Hannibal

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, the evacuation of Germans from Grünhagen began as the war intensified and Soviet forces advanced. This evacuation was part of the larger context of civilian displacements during the war.
events.name: Evacuation of Germans from Grünhagen

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, the MV Wilhelm Gustloff, carrying over 10,000 mainly civilian Germans, was sunk in Gdańsk Bay by Soviet submarine S-13. This tragedy resulted in the greatest loss of life in a single ship sinking in history, with estimates of up to 9,400 casualties.
events.name: Sinking of MV Wilhelm Gustloff

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, a daring raid at Cabanatuan saw 121 American soldiers and 800 Filipino guerrillas successfully free 813 American prisoners of war from a Japanese-held camp. This operation was a significant morale booster for Allied forces in the Philippines.
events.name: Raid at Cabanatuan

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Adolf Hitler delivered his last public speech via broadcast radio, expressing his unwavering belief that Germany would ultimately triumph in the war. This speech reflected his delusions of victory despite the dire situation facing the Third Reich.
events.name: Hitler's last public speech

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, the Soviet Union agreed to enter the Pacific War against Japan once hostilities against Germany were concluded. This decision significantly impacted the post-war balance of power in East Asia.
events.name: Soviet Union's Agreement to Enter Pacific War

events.enhanced_description: On an unspecified date in early 1945, known as 'Black Friday', Allied Bristol Beaufighter aircraft suffered heavy casualties during an unsuccessful attack on German destroyer Z33 and its escorting vessels in Førde Fjord, Norway. This event underscored the dangers faced by Allied forces in their operations against German naval power.
events.name: Black Friday Air Raid

events.enhanced_description: The Budapest Offensive and the Siege of Budapest concluded in early 1945 with Nazi troops surrendering the city to Soviet-Romanian forces. This event marked a significant victory for the Allies in Eastern Europe.
events.name: Siege of Budapest Ends

events.enhanced_description: The Bombing of Dresden occurred in early 1945, executed by the British Royal Air Force and United States Army Air Forces, resulting in an estimated 25,000 to 35,000 deaths. This controversial bombing raid aimed to disrupt German military operations and morale.
events.name: Bombing of Dresden

events.enhanced_description: The Bombing of Wesel began in early 1945, resulting in the destruction of 97% of the town over three days. This bombing was part of the Allied strategy to weaken German defenses as they advanced into Germany.
events.name: Bombing of Wesel

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, American and Filipino ground forces landed on Corregidor Island as part of the campaign to liberate the Philippines from Japanese occupation. This operation was crucial for regaining control of the strategic island.
events.name: Landing on Corregidor Island

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, combined American and Filipino forces successfully recaptured the Bataan Peninsula, a significant strategic victory in the campaign to liberate the Philippines from Japanese forces. This operation was a key part of the broader Allied efforts in the Pacific.
events.name: Recapture of Bataan Peninsula

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, Venezuela officially declared war on Germany, aligning itself with the Allies during World War II. This declaration reflected the growing involvement of Latin American countries in the global conflict.
events.name: Venezuela declares war on Germany

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, Uruguay declared war on both Germany and Japan, joining the Allied efforts during World War II. This decision marked a significant shift in Uruguay's foreign policy during the global conflict.
events.name: Uruguay declares war on Germany and Japan

events.enhanced_description: During the Battle of Iwo Jima, on an unspecified date in early 1945, a group of United States Marines reached the summit of Mount Suribachi and raised the American flag. This iconic moment was captured in a photograph by Joe Rosenthal, which later won a Pulitzer Prize and became a symbol of American valor.

image.caption: U.S. postage stamp commemorating the Battle of Iwo Jima, depicting the flag-raising.
image.credit: US Post Office — US Post Office Hi-res scan of postage stamp by Gwillhickers .
image.date_qualification: The image description identifies a 1945 stamp; the supplied image_date is 1945-07-11. The event photograph was taken on February 23, 1945.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, the 11th Airborne Division, along with Filipino guerrillas, successfully liberated the captives of the Los Baños internment camp. This operation was a significant event in the campaign to free prisoners held by Japanese forces in the Philippines.
events.name: Los Baños Internment Camp Rescue

events.enhanced_description: The German garrison in Poznań surrendered to the advancing Red Army and Polish troops, marking a crucial step in the Soviet offensive in Eastern Europe. This capitulation contributed to the overall collapse of German defenses in Poland.
events.name: Capitulation of German Garrison in Poznań

events.enhanced_description: Henry A. Wallace begins his term as the United States Secretary of Commerce in 1945, serving under President Franklin D. Roosevelt. His tenure is marked by significant economic challenges and the transition towards post-war recovery.
events.name: Henry A. Wallace starts term as Secretary of Commerce

events.enhanced_description: The Bachem Ba 349 Natter, a rocket-propelled interceptor, is first test launched at Stetten am kalten Markt in 1945. The launch ends in tragedy as the pilot, Lothar Sieber, dies during the test.
events.name: First test launch of the Bachem Ba 349 Natter

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Finland formally declares war on the Axis powers, marking a significant shift in its wartime alliances and positioning as World War II draws to a close.
events.name: Finland declares war on the Axis powers

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, United States and Filipino troops successfully capture Manila, the capital of the Philippines, from Japanese forces. This victory is a crucial step in the liberation of the Philippines during World War II.
events.name: United States and Filipino troops take Manila

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, a Polish Home Army unit commits a massacre in the village of Pawłokoma, resulting in the deaths of between 150 and 500 Ukrainian civilians. This event highlights the ethnic tensions and violence during the chaotic aftermath of World War II.
events.name: Pawłokoma massacre

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the British Royal Air Force accidentally bombs the Bezuidenhout neighborhood in The Hague, resulting in the deaths of 511 civilians. This tragic incident underscores the dangers of wartime operations and the impact on civilian populations.
events.name: Bombing of the Bezuidenhout

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Princess Elizabeth, who would later become Queen Elizabeth II, joins the Auxiliary Territorial Service (ATS) as a truck driver and mechanic in London. This marks a significant moment in royal history, showcasing her commitment to the war effort.
events.name: Princess Elizabeth joins the Auxiliary Territorial Service

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the United States accidentally bombs the Swiss cities of Basel and Zürich, causing unintended destruction and highlighting the complexities of wartime operations in neutral countries.
events.name: Accidental bombing of Basel and Zürich

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, a Communist-led government is established in Romania under the leadership of Petru Groza, following significant Soviet intervention. This marks a critical shift in Romanian politics and aligns the country with the Eastern Bloc.
events.name: Formation of Communist-led government in Romania

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Dutch resistance fighters accidentally ambush SS General Hanns Albin Rauter, known for his brutal persecution of the Dutch population. This incident reflects the chaotic and violent atmosphere in the Netherlands during the final months of World War II.
events.name: Ambush of SS General Hanns Albin Rauter

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Josip Broz Tito establishes a Provisional Government of the Democratic Federal Yugoslavia, marking a significant step towards the formation of a socialist federation in the Balkans following World War II.

image.caption: Portrait of Josip Broz Tito in uniform.
image.credit: Unknown author Unknown author — This image is available from the Digital Library of Slovenia under the reference number MJVNDGTF This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing for more information.
image.date_qualification: Portrait of Tito, dated 1961; it is later than the 1945 formation event and is not a contemporary event photograph.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False; Restrictions: communist

events.name: Formation of Provisional Government of Democratic Federal Yugoslavia

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Nazi authorities execute 117 Dutch men in retaliation for the attempted murder of SS General Hanns Albin Rauter. This brutal act exemplifies the harsh reprisals faced by the Dutch resistance during the Nazi occupation.
events.name: Nazi reprisal killings in the Netherlands

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Operation Sunrise sees Waffen-SS General Karl Wolff meet with Allen Welsh Dulles of the United States Office of Strategic Services in Lucerne, Switzerland, to negotiate the surrender of Axis forces in Italy. This clandestine meeting is pivotal in the negotiations for a separate peace.
events.name: Operation Sunrise negotiations

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the Sammarinese general election results in the world's first democratically elected communist government, which will hold power until 1957. This election marks a significant moment in the political history of San Marino.
events.name: Sammarinese general election

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the Bombing of Würzburg, part of the Allied strategic bombing campaign against Nazi Germany, devastates 89% of the city and results in approximately 4,000 deaths. This attack exemplifies the extensive destruction wrought by the war on German cities.
events.name: Bombing of Würzburg

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the 40th Infantry Division, led by the 185th US Infantry Regiment, lands unopposed in Tigbauan, Philippines, leading to the surrender of Japanese forces and the declaration of the Liberation of Panay, Romblon, and Guimaras. This event marks a significant victory for Allied forces in the region.
events.name: Liberation of Panay, Romblon, and Guimaras

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, 1,250 American bombers conduct a massive bombing raid on Berlin, targeting key military and industrial sites. This operation is part of the final Allied offensive against Nazi Germany as the war nears its conclusion.
events.name: American bombing raid on Berlin

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the Battle of Kolberg concludes with Polish and Soviet forces capturing the Baltic seaport, which had been designated a key fortress by the Germans. The battle results in the evacuation or expulsion of ethnic Germans from the area.
events.name: Battle of Kolberg concludes

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Adolf Hitler issues the 'Nero Decree', ordering the destruction of all industries and infrastructure in Germany to prevent their use by advancing Allied forces. However, Albert Speer, tasked with implementing the decree, deliberately disobeys it, reflecting the internal conflicts within the Nazi leadership.
events.name: Hitler's Nero Decree

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, British troops successfully liberated Mandalay, Myanmar, from Japanese occupation during World War II. This strategic victory was part of the larger campaign to reclaim Burma and was crucial for the Allied forces in their efforts to push back Japanese advances in Southeast Asia.
events.name: Liberation of Mandalay

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of the Transdanubian Hills concluded in early 1945 with Bulgarian and Soviet troops successfully defending the north bank of the Drava River. This battle was part of the broader Eastern Front operations during World War II, showcasing the collaboration between Bulgarian and Soviet forces against Axis powers.

locations.name: North bank of the Drava River

events.name: Battle of the Transdanubian Hills

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, Hildesheim, Germany, suffered extensive destruction due to Allied bombing raids, which targeted the city's cathedral and historic center. This bombing was part of the larger Allied strategy to cripple German infrastructure and morale as World War II neared its conclusion.
events.name: Bombing of Hildesheim

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, the United States Army Air Forces initiated Operation Starvation, laying naval mines in various Japanese seaways. This operation aimed to disrupt Japanese shipping and supply lines, significantly impacting Japan's ability to sustain its war efforts during World War II.
events.name: Operation Starvation

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, the Red Army launched a decisive offensive against the German 4th Army in the Heiligenbeil Pocket, located in East Prussia. This battle resulted in the near destruction of the German forces, significantly weakening their position on the Eastern Front as World War II approached its conclusion.
events.name: Heiligenbeil Pocket

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, the Red Army successfully pushed most Axis forces out of Hungary and into Austria during a series of offensives. This maneuver was part of the larger Soviet campaign to liberate Eastern Europe from Axis occupation as World War II neared its end.
events.name: Red Army pushes Axis forces

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, American troops liberated Ohrdruf extermination camp in Germany, marking the first Nazi concentration camp to be freed by U.S. forces. This event highlighted the atrocities committed during the Holocaust.
events.name: Liberation of Ohrdruf

events.enhanced_description: In early April 1945, the Soviet Red Army entered Bratislava and pushed towards Vienna, capturing the city on April 13 after intense fighting. This advance was crucial in the final stages of World War II in Europe.
events.name: Soviet Red Army in Vienna

events.enhanced_description: In April 1945, Sarajevo was liberated from Nazi Germany and the Independent State of Croatia by Yugoslav Partisans, marking a significant moment in the liberation of Yugoslav territories during World War II.
events.name: Liberation of Sarajevo

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Slater's Knoll on Bougainville Island concluded with a decisive victory for the Australian Army's 7th Brigade, contributing to the Allied campaign in the Pacific during World War II.
events.name: Battle of Slater's Knoll

events.enhanced_description: In early April 1945, Allied forces reached the Merkers Salt Mines in Thuringia, uncovering gold reserves of the Nazi German Reichsbank and art treasures. This discovery highlighted the extent of Nazi looting during the war.
events.name: Allied Forces at Merkers Salt Mines

events.enhanced_description: The only flight of the German ramming unit known as Sonderkommando Elbe took place, resulting in the loss of 24 B-17s and B-24s of the United States Eighth Air Force. This mission was a desperate attempt by Germany to counter Allied air superiority.
events.name: Sonderkommando Elbe Mission

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, the Japanese battleship Yamato and nine other warships participated in Operation Ten-Go, a suicide attack on Allied forces engaged in the Battle of Okinawa. The Yamato was sunk by U.S. Navy aircraft, resulting in the loss of over 2,000 crew members.
events.name: Operation Ten-Go

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, Kantarō Suzuki was appointed as Prime Minister of Japan during the final stages of World War II. His leadership came at a critical time as Japan faced increasing pressure from Allied forces.

image.caption: Portrait of Japanese politician and admiral Kantarō Suzuki.
image.credit: Unknown author Unknown author — This image is available from the website of the National Diet Library
image.date_qualification: Portrait of Suzuki, not a depiction of his appointment as prime minister. The image date is qualified as before 1946.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Kantarō Suzuki becomes Prime Minister

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, Abwehr conspirators Wilhelm Canaris, Hans Oster, and Hans von Dohnányi were hanged at Flossenbürg concentration camp, along with pastor Dietrich Bonhoeffer. Their execution highlighted the brutal repression of dissent within Nazi Germany.
events.name: Execution of Abwehr Conspirators

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, Johann Georg Elser, the would-be assassin of Adolf Hitler, was executed at Dachau concentration camp. His assassination attempt was a significant act of resistance against the Nazi regime.
events.name: Execution of Johann Georg Elser

events.enhanced_description: In early 1945, rocket scientist Wernher von Braun and 120 members of his team surrendered to U.S. forces in Lübeck, Germany. This pivotal moment marked the beginning of their contributions to the U.S. space program, significantly advancing rocket technology.
events.name: Wernher von Braun and team surrender to U.S. forces

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, German Protestant theologian Gerhard Kittel was arrested by French forces in Tübingen, Germany. Kittel was known for his controversial theological views and his involvement in the Nazi regime, which led to his arrest at the end of World War II.
events.name: Gerhard Kittel arrested by French forces

events.enhanced_description: Operation Dracula was a military campaign in April 1945 where British troops successfully liberated the Burmese capital of Rangoon from Japanese occupation. This operation was crucial in restoring Allied control over Burma and contributed to the overall defeat of Japan in Southeast Asia.
events.name: Operation Dracula: Liberation of Rangoon

events.enhanced_description: In May 1945, British and Canadian troops liberated the Netherlands from Nazi occupation, culminating in the liberation of Amsterdam. This event was celebrated by the Dutch as a significant moment of freedom after years of oppression during World War II.
events.name: Liberation of the Netherlands

events.enhanced_description: Denmark was liberated in May 1945 as German forces capitulated at the end of World War II. The liberation was celebrated nationwide, marking the end of five years of occupation.

locations.name: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark

events.name: Liberation of Denmark

events.enhanced_description: In May 1945, Admiral Karl Dönitz ordered all German U-boats to cease offensive operations and return to their bases in Norway. This order signified the collapse of German naval operations as World War II came to an end.
events.name: Admiral Dönitz orders U-boats to cease operations

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the Holy Crown of Hungary was discovered by the United States Army's 86th Infantry Division in Mattsee, Austria. The crown was subsequently kept in Fort Knox for safekeeping until it was returned to Hungary in 1978.
events.name: Discovery of the Holy Crown of Hungary

events.enhanced_description: In May 1945, the German auxiliary cruiser Orion sank while carrying refugees to Copenhagen, resulting in the tragic loss of over 3,800 lives. This incident highlighted the chaos and desperation of the final days of World War II in Europe.

locations.name: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark

events.name: Sinking of German auxiliary cruiser Orion

events.enhanced_description: In May 1945, the Prague uprising erupted as citizens rose against occupying Nazi forces, spurred by radio broadcasts. This uprising led to intense fighting, including the Battle for Czech Radio, and was a significant moment in the liberation of Czechoslovakia.
events.name: Prague uprising against Nazi forces

events.enhanced_description: In early May 1945, Canadian soldiers liberated Amsterdam from Nazi occupation, marking a significant moment in the Netherlands' liberation. The event was celebrated by the Dutch population, symbolizing the end of years of suffering under Nazi rule.
events.name: Liberation of Amsterdam

events.enhanced_description: In May 1945, a Japanese fire balloon exploded near Bly, Oregon, killing six people, including Elsie Mitchell and five children. This incident marked the only fatalities on the American mainland due to enemy action during World War II.
events.name: Japanese fire balloon incident in Oregon

events.enhanced_description: On May 1, 1945, Mildred Gillars, known as 'Axis Sally', delivered her last propaganda broadcast to Allied troops during World War II. Her broadcasts aimed to demoralize American soldiers and were part of the psychological warfare employed by the Nazis.
events.name: Mildred Gillars delivers last propaganda broadcast

events.enhanced_description: In May 1945, numerous RAF Lancasters landed in Germany to repatriate British prisoners of war. Over the next 24 hours, approximately 4,500 ex-POWs were flown back to Great Britain, marking a significant step in the post-war recovery.
events.name: RAF Lancasters repatriate British POWs

events.enhanced_description: In May 1945, the surrender of the Dodecanese was signed in Symi, marking the end of hostilities in the region. This event was part of the broader context of the end of World War II in Europe.

image.caption: Locator map of the Dodecanese prefecture in Greece.
image.credit: Pitichinaccio — Own work
image.date_qualification: Map dated 2007-12-21; it is not a contemporary image of the 1945 surrender.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Surrender of the Dodecanese signed in Symi

events.enhanced_description: The Prague uprising, which began in early May 1945, ended with a ceasefire as the city was liberated from Nazi occupation. This uprising was a significant moment in Czechoslovakia's struggle for freedom.
events.name: Ceasefire of the Prague uprising

events.enhanced_description: In May 1945, the Eighth British Army, along with Slovene partisan troops, arrived in Carinthia and Klagenfurt. This movement was part of the broader context of the end of World War II in Europe and the shifting power dynamics in the region.
events.name: Eighth British Army arrives in Carinthia

events.enhanced_description: On May 8, 1945, Hermann Göring surrendered to the United States Army near Radstadt, Austria. As a leading figure in the Nazi regime, his capture marked a significant moment in the aftermath of World War II.
events.name: Hermann Göring surrenders to the United States Army

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Vidkun Quisling, the leader of Norway's collaborationist regime during World War II, surrendered to the Norwegian Resistance (Milorg) and police at Møllergata 19 in Oslo. This event marked a significant step in the legal purge of collaborators following the end of the war in Europe.
events.name: Surrender of Vidkun Quisling and the Quisling regime

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, General Alexander Löhr, the commander of German Army Group E, signed the capitulation of German occupation troops near Topolšica, Slovenia. This surrender was part of the broader collapse of German forces in Eastern Europe as World War II neared its conclusion.
events.name: Capitulation of German Army Group E

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, British forces liberated the German-occupied Channel Islands, marking the end of a five-year occupation. Royal Navy ships HMS Bulldog and HMS Beagle played key roles in the surrender of occupying troops in St Peter Port, Guernsey, and St Helier, Jersey, respectively.
events.name: Liberation of the Channel Islands

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Heinrich Himmler, the former head of the Nazi SS, committed suicide while in British custody. His death marked a significant moment in the aftermath of World War II, as he was one of the key figures responsible for the Holocaust.
events.name: Heinrich Himmler's suicide

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Dutch painter Han van Meegeren was arrested for collaborating with the Nazis by selling forged Dutch Golden Age paintings to Hermann Göring. His arrest highlighted the complexities of art, identity, and collaboration during the war.
events.name: Arrest of Han van Meegeren

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, the Franck Committee recommended against a surprise nuclear bombing of Japan, advocating instead for a demonstration of the atomic bomb's power. This recommendation highlighted the ethical concerns surrounding the use of nuclear weapons.
events.name: Franck Committee's recommendation against nuclear bombing

events.enhanced_description: The Provisional International Civil Aviation Organization (PICAO) was established to promote the safe and orderly development of international civil aviation. It was a precursor to the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), which was formally established in 1947.
events.name: The Provisional International Civil Aviation Organization is founded, as a specialized agency of the United Nations

events.enhanced_description: On this date, the United States conducted a bombing raid on Kumagaya, Japan, using conventional bombs. This attack was part of a broader strategy to weaken Japanese military capabilities during World War II.
events.name: Bombing of Kumagaya, Japan, by the United States

events.enhanced_description: President José P. Laurel issued an Executive Proclamation to officially end the Second Philippine Republic, marking the conclusion of his presidency. This event occurred in the context of the Philippines transitioning back to American control after Japanese occupation.
events.name: Philippines President José P. Laurel issues an Executive Proclamation

events.enhanced_description: Field Marshal Walther von Brauchitsch, who served as Commander-in-Chief of the German Army during the early years of World War II, was arrested by Allied troops. His capture symbolized the collapse of the Nazi military leadership.
events.name: WWII: Allied troops arrest German field marshal Walther von Brauchitsch

events.enhanced_description: At American Cyanamid's Lederle Laboratories in Pearl River, New York, a team led by Yellapragada Subbarow successfully isolated folic acid in a pure crystalline form. This discovery was significant for nutritional science and public health.
events.name: Folic acid obtained in pure crystalline form

events.enhanced_description: General Douglas MacArthur was appointed as the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers in Japan, overseeing the occupation and reconstruction of the country following its defeat in World War II. His leadership was pivotal in shaping post-war Japan.
events.name: General Douglas MacArthur appointed Supreme Commander Allied Powers

events.enhanced_description: Igor Gouzenko, a Russian code clerk, came forward with documents revealing extensive Soviet espionage activities in North America. His revelations marked the beginning of the Cold War and heightened tensions between the East and West.
events.name: Igor Gouzenko exposes Soviet espionage

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Japanese troops formally relinquished control over Southern Korea to the United States, marking the end of Japan's 35-year rule over the Korean Peninsula. This event was a significant step in the post-World War II reorganization of East Asia.
events.name: Japanese troops in Keijō formally relinquish control over Southern Korea

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Radio Republik Indonesia commenced its broadcasts, marking a significant development in Indonesian media and communication during the struggle for independence from colonial rule. This station played a crucial role in disseminating information and fostering national identity.
events.name: Radio Republik Indonesia starts broadcasting

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, Australian forces liberated the Batu Lintang camp in Sarawak, Borneo, which had been used by the Japanese to detain prisoners of war and civilians. This liberation was part of the broader Allied campaign to reclaim territories occupied by Japan during World War II.
events.name: Batu Lintang camp liberated

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, the Japanese Army formally surrendered to British forces in Singapore, marking a pivotal moment in the conclusion of World War II in Southeast Asia. This surrender symbolized the collapse of Japanese military power in the region.
events.name: Japanese Army formally surrenders to the British

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, the United States Army Military Government in Korea disbanded the office of the governor-general of Korea, effectively ending Japan's 35-year rule. This marked the beginning of a new era in Korean governance and the eventual establishment of an independent Korean state.
events.name: Disbanding of the governor-general of Korea

events.enhanced_description: In early January 1945, Typhoon Makurazaki struck Japan, resulting in the tragic loss of 3,746 lives. This natural disaster highlighted the vulnerability of the Japanese population during a time of war and devastation.
events.name: Typhoon Makurazaki

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1945, the Japanese Army in Central China officially surrendered to Chinese forces in Wuhan. This event marked a significant turning point in the Chinese resistance against Japanese occupation during World War II.
events.name: Japanese Army surrenders in Central China

events.enhanced_description: In January 1945, Arthur C. Clarke published an article in Wireless World magazine proposing the concept of a geosynchronous communications satellite. This groundbreaking idea laid the foundation for modern satellite communications and changed the landscape of global communication.
events.name: Arthur C. Clarke proposes geosynchronous satellite

events.enhanced_description: The International Court of Justice was established on January 1, 1945, as the principal judicial organ of the United Nations. It was created to settle legal disputes between states and provide advisory opinions on international legal issues.
events.name: The International Court of Justice is established by the United Nations Charter

events.enhanced_description: Vidkun Quisling, the infamous Norwegian collaborator with Nazi Germany, was executed by firing squad for treason on January 1, 1945. His name has since become synonymous with betrayal and collaboration.
events.name: Norwegian Nazi leader Vidkun Quisling is executed by firing squad

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Getúlio Vargas was deposed from the presidency of Brazil, leading to José Linhares being appointed as the temporary president. This political upheaval was part of a broader movement towards democratization in Brazil.
events.name: Getúlio Vargas is deposed as president in Brazil; José Linhares is named temporary president

events.enhanced_description: The Osijek prison massacre occurred in 1945 when the Yugoslav secret police executed numerous political prisoners. This event highlighted the violent repression of dissent in post-war Yugoslavia.
events.name: Osijek prison massacre by Yugoslav secret police

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Gimbels Department Store in New York City became the first retailer to sell ballpoint pens, priced at $12. This marked a significant innovation in writing technology, making writing instruments more accessible and practical.
events.name: At Gimbels Department Store in New York City, the first ballpoint pens go on sale at $12

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Telechron introduced the model 8H59 Musalarm, recognized as the first clock radio, which combined a clock and radio into a single device. This innovation revolutionized how people interacted with time and media in their homes.
events.name: Telechron introduces the model 8H59 Musalarm, the first clock radio

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the Kuomintang launched an offensive in Manchuria against the Chinese Communist Party, marking a significant escalation in the Chinese Civil War. This conflict would shape the future of China and lead to the establishment of the People's Republic of China.
events.name: An offensive is begun in Manchuria by the Kuomintang

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Charles de Gaulle was unanimously elected president of France by the provisional government, solidifying his leadership role in post-war France. His presidency would lay the groundwork for the establishment of the French Fifth Republic.
events.name: Charles de Gaulle is unanimously elected president of France

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the United States controversially imported 88 German scientists as part of Operation Paperclip to aid in the development of rocket technology. This decision sparked ethical debates regarding the use of former Nazi scientists in American military and space programs.
events.name: The United States controversially imports 88 German scientists

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the foundation of UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) was agreed upon during a meeting in London, aiming to promote international collaboration in education, science, and culture. This organization plays a crucial role in fostering peace and security through educational initiatives.
events.name: The foundation of UNESCO is agreed

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, a devastating earthquake struck Balochistan, Pakistan, triggering a tsunami that resulted in the deaths of approximately 4,000 people. This natural disaster highlighted the region's vulnerability to seismic activity.
events.name: Balochistan earthquake causes a tsunami and kills 4,000

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, British fascist John Amery pleaded guilty to treason and was subsequently condemned to death. His trial was emblematic of the post-war reckoning with collaborators and traitors in the United Kingdom.
events.name: British fascist John Amery pleads guilty to treason

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, the assembly of the Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer (ENIAC), the world's first general-purpose electronic computer, was completed at the University of Pennsylvania. This groundbreaking achievement marked the beginning of the computer age, enabling complex calculations and simulations.

locations.name: University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States

events.name: Assembly of the world's first general purpose electronic computer, ENIAC, is completed

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, several major French banks, including the Bank of France and Crédit Lyonnais, were nationalized as part of the post-war economic restructuring. This move aimed to stabilize the financial system and promote economic recovery in France.
events.name: French banks are nationalized

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, a team led by Charles Coryell at Oak Ridge National Laboratory discovered chemical element 61, which they named promethium. This discovery filled the last gap in the periodic table between elements 1 and 96, although it was not publicly announced until 1947.
events.name: A team at Oak Ridge National Laboratory discovers chemical element 61, promethium

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Klamath Falls, Oregon, became the site of the first geothermal milk pasteurization, utilizing the region's geothermal resources to enhance food safety and preservation. This innovative technique showcased the potential of geothermal energy in agricultural practices.
events.name: The first geothermal milk pasteurization is done

events.enhanced_description: On January 2, 1946, Japanese General Tomoyuki Yamashita surrendered to Philippine and American forces in Kiangan, Ifugao. His surrender marked the end of organized Japanese resistance in the Philippines.
events.name: Japanese general Tomoyuki Yamashita surrenders

events.enhanced_description: On January 6, 1945, a German offensive successfully recaptured Esztergom, Hungary from Soviet forces. This event was part of the larger struggle for control over Hungary during the final stages of World War II.
events.name: German offensive recaptures Esztergom

events.enhanced_description: On January 9, 1945, American and Australian troops landed at Lingayen Gulf on the western coast of Luzon, Philippines, which had been occupied by Japan since 1942. This landing was a crucial step in the liberation of the Philippines from Japanese control.
events.name: American and Australian troops land at Lingayen Gulf

events.enhanced_description: On January 12, 1945, the Soviet Union launched the Vistula–Oder Offensive in Eastern Europe against the German Army. This major military operation aimed to push German forces back and was a significant step towards the eventual Soviet advance into Germany.
events.name: Soviet Union begins Vistula–Oder Offensive

events.enhanced_description: On January 13, 1945, the Soviet Union commenced the East Prussian Offensive, aiming to eliminate German forces in East Prussia. This offensive was part of the broader strategy to weaken German military capabilities as the war neared its conclusion.

image.caption: Map of the East Prussian offensive.
image.credit: Mil.ru — http://mil.ru/winner_may/history/more.htm?id=12006377@cmsArticle
image.date_qualification: Map dated 2011-02-10; it is a later map, not a contemporary photograph of the 1945 offensive.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Soviet Union begins East Prussian Offensive

events.enhanced_description: On January 16, 1945, Adolf Hitler took residence in the Führerbunker in Berlin. This underground bunker would serve as his last refuge as the Allies closed in on the city, marking a significant moment in the final days of the Third Reich.
events.name: Adolf Hitler takes residence in the Führerbunker

events.enhanced_description: On January 17, 1945, the Soviet Union occupied Warsaw, Poland. This occupation was a pivotal moment in the liberation of Poland from Nazi control and marked a significant advance of Soviet forces into Central Europe.
events.name: Soviet Union occupies Warsaw

events.enhanced_description: On January 18, 1945, the SS began the evacuation of Auschwitz concentration camp, forcing nearly 60,000 prisoners, primarily Jews, to march to other locations in Germany. Tragically, as many as 15,000 died during this brutal forced march, while 7,000 too sick to move were left behind without supplies.
events.name: Evacuation of Auschwitz concentration camp

events.enhanced_description: On January 19, 1945, Soviet forces liberated the Łódź Ghetto, where only 877 Jews remained from an initial population of 164,000. This liberation was a stark reminder of the devastating impact of the Holocaust on Jewish communities in Poland.
events.name: Liberation of the Łódź Ghetto

events.enhanced_description: On January 20, 1945, Franklin D. Roosevelt was sworn in for a fourth term as President of the United States, making him the only president in U.S. history to serve more than two terms. His unprecedented tenure reflected the extraordinary circumstances of World War II.
events.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt's fourth inauguration

events.enhanced_description: On the night of January 21, 1945, two trains collided at the Grünhagen railroad station in East Prussia, resulting in the deaths of between 140 and 150 people. The station was subsequently destroyed by advancing Soviet forces at dawn.
events.name: Train collision at Grünhagen railroad station

events.enhanced_description: On January 24, 1945, AP war correspondent Joseph Morton, along with nine OSS men and four SOE agents, were executed by the Germans at Mauthausen concentration camp. Morton was notably the only Allied correspondent executed by the Axis during the war, under Hitler's Commando Order.
events.name: Execution of Joseph Morton and others at Mauthausen

events.enhanced_description: On January 25, 1945, Adolf Hitler appointed Heinrich Himmler, who lacked military experience, as the commander of the newly formed Army Group Vistula. This decision was part of a desperate attempt to halt the advancing Soviet Red Army during the Vistula–Oder offensive.
events.name: Hitler appoints Heinrich Himmler as commander of Army Group Vistula

events.enhanced_description: On January 25, 1945, the highly anticipated basketball game known as the 'Clash of Titans' took place at Madison Square Garden in New York City, featuring star players George Mikan and Bob Kurland. The game ended with Oklahoma State University defeating DePaul University 52-44, showcasing the growing popularity of college basketball in America.
events.name: Clash of Titans basketball game

events.enhanced_description: On January 26, 1945, 19-year-old U.S. Army Staff Sergeant Audie Murphy distinguished himself in combat at Holtzwihr, France. His bravery during the battle earned him the Medal of Honor, making him one of the most decorated American combat soldiers of World War II.
events.name: Audie Murphy sees action at Holtzwihr

events.enhanced_description: On January 27, 1945, the Soviet Red Army liberated the Auschwitz and Birkenau concentration camps, uncovering the horrific conditions and the atrocities committed against the Jewish population and other prisoners during the Holocaust.

image.caption: Auschwitz I barracks, at the former German concentration camp in Oświęcim, Poland.
image.credit: File:Auschwitz I (22 May 2010).jpg : xiquinhosilva derivative work: Georgfotoart — This file was derived from: Auschwitz I (22 May 2010).jpg :
image.date_qualification: Photographed 22 May 2010; depicts the site, not the liberation in 1945.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Liberation of Auschwitz and Birkenau

events.enhanced_description: On January 30, 1945, significant military actions occurred in the Baltic Sea as World War II continued to escalate. This period was marked by naval engagements and the movement of troops and supplies.
events.name: Baltic Sea incident

events.enhanced_description: On January 31, 1945, the Battle of Hill 170 concluded with the British 3rd Commando Brigade defeating the Imperial Japanese Army's 54th Division. This victory forced the Japanese Twenty-Eighth Army to withdraw from the strategically important Arakan Peninsula.
events.name: Battle of Hill 170

events.enhanced_description: On January 31, 1945, the cartoon character Sylvester the Cat made his debut in the animated short 'Life with Feathers.' Created by Friz Freleng and voiced by Mel Blanc, Sylvester quickly became a beloved character in the Looney Tunes franchise, known for his catchphrase 'Sufferin' succotash!'
events.name: Debut of Sylvester the Cat

events.enhanced_description: In February 1945, Raymond L. Libby of American Cyanamid's research laboratories in Stamford, Connecticut, announced a groundbreaking method for orally administering the antibiotic penicillin. This innovation significantly improved the accessibility and effectiveness of this life-saving drug.
events.name: Announcement of penicillin administration method

events.enhanced_description: On February 4, 1945, President Franklin D. Roosevelt, Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin convened at the Yalta Conference to discuss the post-war reorganization of Europe. This meeting was crucial in shaping the geopolitical landscape following World War II.
events.name: Yalta Conference

events.enhanced_description: On February 7, 1945, General Douglas MacArthur returned to Manila, Philippines, fulfilling his promise to liberate the country from Japanese occupation. His return marked a pivotal moment in the liberation of the Philippines during World War II.
events.name: MacArthur returns to Manila

events.enhanced_description: On February 8, 1945, the Alaska Anti-Discrimination Act was passed by the territorial Senate, championed by native leader Elizabeth Peratrovich. This landmark legislation aimed to combat racial discrimination and was a significant step towards civil rights in Alaska.
events.name: Alaska Anti-Discrimination Act

events.enhanced_description: In 1945, Walter Ulbricht became the leader of the German Communists in Moscow, a pivotal role during a time of significant political change in post-war Europe. His leadership would influence the direction of communist ideology in Germany.
events.name: Walter Ulbricht becomes leader of German Communists

events.enhanced_description: On February 10, 1945, the German troopship SS General von Steuben was sunk by the Soviet submarine S-13 in the Baltic Sea, resulting in the drowning of 3,608 individuals. This incident highlighted the perilous conditions faced by German forces and civilians during the final stages of the war.
events.name: Sinking of SS General von Steuben

events.enhanced_description: On February 10, 1945, Operation Kita was executed by the Imperial Japanese Navy, successfully returning the 'Completion Force', which included Ise-class battleships, from Singapore to Kure, Japan. This operation was conducted despite ongoing Allied attacks.
events.name: Operation Kita

events.enhanced_description: On February 11, 1945, Alger Hiss was congratulated in Moscow for his role in facilitating discussions between Western powers and the Soviet Union during the Yalta Conference. This conference was pivotal in shaping post-war Europe and establishing the framework for international relations in the years to come.
events.name: Alger Hiss at Yalta Conference

events.enhanced_description: On February 12, 1945, a devastating tornado outbreak struck Mississippi and Alabama, resulting in the deaths of 45 individuals and injuring 427 others. The outbreak caused widespread destruction across multiple towns, highlighting the severe impact of tornadoes in the region.
events.name: Tornado outbreak in Mississippi and Alabama

events.enhanced_description: On February 19, 1945, during World War II, a controversial incident occurred on Ramree Island where Japanese soldiers were reportedly attacked by saltwater crocodiles. Estimates of casualties vary widely, with figures ranging from 20 to 980, highlighting the chaotic nature of warfare and the unpredictability of natural threats.
events.name: Ramree Island crocodile attacks

events.enhanced_description: On February 19, 1945, approximately 30,000 United States Marines landed on Iwo Jima as part of a crucial offensive during World War II. This battle was significant for its strategic importance and the fierce resistance encountered from Japanese forces.
events.name: Battle of Iwo Jima

events.enhanced_description: On February 21, 1945, the last V-2 rocket was launched from Peenemünde, marking the end of an era for Germany's advanced weaponry during World War II. The V-2 rocket program was a significant technological achievement, despite its use in warfare.
events.name: Last V-2 rocket launch

events.enhanced_description: The liberation of Manila marked a significant event in World War II, as American and Filipino forces fought to reclaim the capital from Japanese occupation. The battle resulted in extensive destruction, particularly in the historic district of Intramuros, and led to a high civilian death toll.
events.name: Liberation of Manila

events.enhanced_description: The bombing of Pforzheim by the British Royal Air Force was one of the most devastating air raids of World War II, resulting in the deaths of approximately 17,600 civilians and the destruction of a significant portion of the city. This raid exemplified the intense aerial bombardment strategy employed by the Allies against German cities.
events.name: Bombing of Pforzheim

events.enhanced_description: Turkey officially joined the Allies in World War II, marking a significant shift in its foreign policy. This decision was influenced by the changing dynamics of the war and the desire to secure a post-war position in Europe.
events.name: Turkey joins World War II

events.enhanced_description: On February 24, 1945, Egyptian Premier Ahmad Mahir Pasha was assassinated in Parliament shortly after declaring war on Germany and Japan. His assassination marked a significant political upheaval in Egypt during a tumultuous period of World War II.
events.name: Assassination of Ahmad Mahir Pasha

events.enhanced_description: On February 27, 1945, the Bombing of Mainz resulted in 1,209 confirmed deaths and the destruction of 80% of the city. This air raid was part of the Allied strategy to cripple German infrastructure as World War II neared its end.
events.name: Bombing of Mainz

events.enhanced_description: On February 28, 1945, a violent demonstration occurred in Bucharest, where a Bolshevik group opened fire on the army and protesters. In response, Andrei Y. Vishinsky, the USSR vice commissioner of foreign affairs, intervened to compel Nicolae Rădescu to resign as premier, reflecting the intense political tensions in Romania during this period.
events.name: Bucharest Demonstration

events.enhanced_description: President Franklin D. Roosevelt delivered his final address to Congress, discussing the outcomes of the Yalta Conference and the ongoing war efforts. This address was significant as it reflected Roosevelt's vision for post-war peace and cooperation.
events.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt's Last Address

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Iwo Jima unofficially ends in early 1945, following intense fighting between American and Japanese forces. The battle was crucial for the Allies as it provided a strategic base for air operations against the Japanese mainland.
events.name: Battle of Iwo Jima unofficially ends

events.enhanced_description: Henry A. Wallace was appointed as the Secretary of Commerce under President Franklin D. Roosevelt, taking on a crucial role in managing the economic policies of the United States during the final stages of World War II.
events.name: Henry A. Wallace becomes Secretary of Commerce

events.enhanced_description: Following Soviet intervention, a Communist-led government was established in Romania under the leadership of Petru Groza. This marked a significant shift in Romanian politics and aligned the country more closely with Soviet interests during the early Cold War.
events.name: Formation of Communist Government in Romania

events.enhanced_description: Operation Lumberjack culminated in the capture of the Ludendorff Bridge at Remagen by American forces, allowing for the rapid crossing of troops and equipment into Germany. This strategic victory was pivotal in the Allied advance towards Berlin.
events.name: Operation Lumberjack

events.enhanced_description: The Salussola massacre on March 9, 1945, involved the execution of partisans by Nazi soldiers in Italy. This event exemplified the brutal reprisals against resistance fighters in the final stages of World War II.
events.name: Salussola massacre

events.enhanced_description: The bombing of Tokyo by USAAF B-29 bombers resulted in catastrophic destruction and loss of life, with estimates of civilian casualties reaching 100,000. This event was one of the most devastating air raids of World War II, showcasing the destructive power of incendiary bombing.
events.name: Bombing of Tokyo

events.enhanced_description: The Empire of Japan established the Empire of Vietnam, a puppet state led by Bảo Đại, during World War II. This regime was short-lived, lasting only until August 23, as Japanese control weakened and nationalist movements gained momentum.
events.name: Establishment of the Empire of Vietnam

events.enhanced_description: The USAAF conducted a devastating bombing raid on Swinemünde, resulting in the deaths of thousands of civilians, many of whom were refugees. This attack highlighted the tragic consequences of war on non-combatants.
events.name: Destruction of Swinemünde

events.enhanced_description: The Upper Silesian Offensive was a major military operation conducted by the Soviet Red Army, aimed at liberating Upper Silesia from German control. This offensive was part of the broader strategy to push into Germany and contributed to the eventual defeat of Nazi forces.
events.name: Upper Silesian Offensive

events.enhanced_description: The 17th Academy Awards ceremony was notable for being the first to be broadcast via radio in the United States. The film 'Going My Way' won the Best Picture award, reflecting the cultural impact of cinema during the war years.
events.name: 17th Academy Awards

events.enhanced_description: The firebombing of Kobe by USAAF B-29 bombers resulted in significant destruction and loss of life, with over 8,000 casualties. This attack was part of the broader strategy of incendiary bombing against Japanese cities during World War II.
events.name: Kobe Firebombing

events.enhanced_description: On March 19, 1945, the aircraft carrier USS Franklin was struck by bombs from Japanese aircraft while operating off the coast of Japan. The attack resulted in the deaths of approximately 800 crew members and severely damaged the ship, marking one of the most devastating attacks on a U.S. naval vessel during World War II.

image.caption: Bow of the aircraft carrier USS Franklin (CV-13), anchored in lower New York Harbor for battle-damage repairs.
image.credit: U.S. Navy — Official U.S. Navy photo 80-G-K-4775 from the U.S. Navy Naval History and Heritage Command
image.date_qualification: Photographed 1945-04-28, after the March 19, 1945 attack; this is an aftermath image, not a photograph of the attack itself.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Attack on USS Franklin

events.enhanced_description: Adolf Hitler dismissed Heinrich Himmler from his military command, reflecting the internal strife and power struggles within the Nazi leadership as the war turned against Germany. This decision marked a significant moment in the waning days of the Third Reich.
events.name: Heinrich Himmler Dismissed

events.enhanced_description: On March 22, 1945, the Arab League was formed in Cairo, Egypt, with the adoption of its charter. This organization aimed to promote political, economic, cultural, and social cooperation among Arab states, marking a significant step towards regional unity in the Arab world.
events.name: Formation of the Arab League

events.enhanced_description: On March 24, 1945, Operation Varsity was launched, involving two airborne divisions capturing key bridges across the Rhine River to facilitate the Allied advance into Germany. This operation was one of the largest airborne assaults in history and played a crucial role in the final stages of World War II in Europe.
events.name: Operation Varsity

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Iwo Jima officially concludes on March 26, 1945, marking a pivotal moment in the Pacific Theater of World War II. Despite the official end, some Japanese holdouts remained on the island until 1949, illustrating the fierce resistance faced by Allied forces.
events.name: Battle of Iwo Jima officially ends

events.enhanced_description: On March 27, 1945, Argentina officially declared war on Germany and Japan, aligning itself with the Allied powers during the final stages of World War II. This declaration marked a significant shift in Argentina's foreign policy and contributed to the global effort against the Axis powers.
events.name: Argentina declares war

events.enhanced_description: On March 29, 1945, the Red Army nearly annihilates the German 4th Army in the Heiligenbeil Pocket during the final stages of World War II in Europe. This decisive engagement contributes significantly to the collapse of German defenses in East Prussia.
events.name: Red Army's assault on the Heiligenbeil Pocket

events.enhanced_description: On April 1, 1945, the Tenth United States Army landed on Okinawa, marking the beginning of one of the largest and bloodiest battles in the Pacific Theater during World War II. The battle lasted for several months and was crucial for the Allied forces in their campaign to invade the Japanese mainland.

image.caption: U.S. Marines celebrate Victory over Japan Day on Okinawa.
image.credit: USMC Archives from Quantico, USA — V-J Day Celebration, Okinawa, August 1945
image.date_qualification: August 1945; the depicted celebration is after the battle, which ended on 22 June 1945.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Battle of Okinawa

events.enhanced_description: In April 1945, the British 3rd Infantry Division, under the command of General Whistler, successfully captured the strategic port city of Bremen from German forces. This victory was part of the broader Allied campaign to liberate Germany from Nazi control.
events.name: Capture of Bremen

events.enhanced_description: In April 1945, the provisional government of Austria, led by Karl Renner, declared its independence from Germany. This assertion was a pivotal moment in Austria's post-war recovery and reestablishment as a sovereign nation.
events.name: Austria's Independence Assertion

events.enhanced_description: In April 1945, U.S. Ordnance troops discovered the coffins of notable historical figures, including Frederick William I of Prussia and Frederick the Great, in a salt mine in Germany. This discovery highlighted the remnants of Germany's imperial past amidst the chaos of World War II.
events.name: Discovery of Historical Coffins

events.enhanced_description: In April 1945, Brazilian forces successfully liberated the commune of Fornovo di Taro from German occupation. This operation was part of the broader Allied efforts to reclaim Italian territory from Axis powers.
events.name: Liberation of Fornovo di Taro

events.enhanced_description: In April 1945, British Avro Lancaster bombers conducted Operation Manna, dropping food supplies into the Netherlands to alleviate the starvation of the civilian population during the German occupation. This humanitarian effort was crucial in saving countless lives.
events.name: Operation Manna

events.enhanced_description: On April 8, 1945, as the Allies advanced, the SS began evacuating the Buchenwald concentration camp. In a remarkable act of resistance, inmates overpowered and killed the remaining guards, marking a significant moment in the struggle for survival and liberation during the Holocaust.
events.name: Buchenwald evacuation

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Königsberg concluded on April 9, 1945, with Soviet forces capturing the city from German defenders. This battle was part of the larger Soviet offensive in East Prussia and marked a significant victory for the Red Army as they pushed deeper into German territory.
events.name: Battle of Königsberg

events.enhanced_description: On April 10, 1945, the town of Visoko was liberated by the 7th, 9th, and 17th Krajina Brigades from the Tenth Division of Yugoslav Partisan forces. This liberation was part of the broader efforts of the Partisans to free Yugoslavia from Axis occupation during World War II.
events.name: Liberation of Visoko

events.enhanced_description: On April 11, 1945, the United States Army liberated the Buchenwald concentration camp, uncovering the horrific conditions and atrocities committed against the inmates. This liberation was a pivotal moment in the Holocaust, bringing international attention to the crimes of the Nazi regime.
events.name: Liberation of Buchenwald

events.enhanced_description: On April 12, 1945, Vice President Harry S. Truman was sworn in as the 33rd president of the United States following the death of President Franklin D. Roosevelt from a cerebral hemorrhage at the Little White House in Warm Springs, Georgia. Truman's presidency would lead the nation through the final months of World War II and the beginning of the Cold War.
events.name: Harry S. Truman becomes President

events.enhanced_description: Harry S. Truman ascended to the presidency of the United States following the death of Franklin D. Roosevelt from a cerebral hemorrhage at the Little White House in Warm Springs, Georgia. Truman was sworn in later that evening at the White House, marking the beginning of his presidency during a critical time in American history.
events.name: Vice President Harry S

events.enhanced_description: A devastating tornado outbreak swept across the United States, resulting in the deaths of 128 individuals and injuring over 1,000 others. This tragic event occurred on the same day as the death of President Roosevelt, overshadowing the disaster in the national consciousness.
events.name: Tornado outbreak in the United States

events.enhanced_description: During World War II, the U.S. Ninth Army, commanded by General William H. Simpson, successfully crossed the Elbe River near Magdeburg, advancing towards Tangermünde and coming within 50 miles of Berlin. This maneuver was a significant step in the Allied push into Germany.
events.name: WWII: The U.S. Ninth Army crosses the Elbe River

events.enhanced_description: Renowned composer Richard Strauss completed his composition 'Metamorphosen' in 1945, a poignant reflection on the destruction of culture and art during World War II. The piece is often interpreted as a lament for the loss of the world Strauss knew.

image.caption: Portrait of Richard Strauss in Garmisch-Partenkirchen.
image.credit: Stindt. Kameramann des Special Film Project 186 der United States Army Air Forces (USAAF) — Screenshot aus: Welche Farbe hat der Krieg? Spiegel TV, 2000. Teil 2 bei 54:15 (VHS)
image.date_qualification: Image metadata dates the depicted material to 1945; this is not a date for a specific completion event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Richard Strauss completes Metamorphosen

events.enhanced_description: The First Canadian Army took military control of the Netherlands, effectively trapping German forces in the Atlantic Wall fortifications along the coastline. This strategic move was part of the broader Allied efforts to liberate Western Europe.
events.name: First Canadian Army assumes control of the Netherlands

events.enhanced_description: The 4th Canadian (Armoured) Division, under the orders of Major General Christopher Vokes, deliberately razed the German town of Friesoythe. This action was part of the military strategy during the liberation of the Netherlands and the push against German forces.
events.name: Razing of Friesoythe

events.enhanced_description: British and Canadian forces liberated the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, revealing the horrific conditions and the extent of the atrocities committed during the Holocaust. This liberation became a significant moment in the Allied efforts to confront the realities of Nazi crimes.
events.name: Liberation of Bergen-Belsen concentration camp

events.enhanced_description: The Canadian First Army successfully captured Arnhem, a strategic city in the northern Netherlands, as part of their campaign to liberate the country from German occupation. This victory was crucial in the broader context of the Allied advance into Germany.
events.name: Canadian First Army captures Arnhem

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Berlin commenced as the Red Army launched a major offensive, initiating the Battle of the Oder–Neisse and the Battle of the Seelow Heights. This marked the final assault on the German capital, leading to the end of World War II in Europe.
events.name: Battle of Berlin begins

events.enhanced_description: Canadian forces successfully occupied the cities of Leeuwarden and Groningen in the Netherlands, contributing to the liberation of the country from German occupation. This operation was part of the larger Allied campaign in Western Europe.
events.name: Canadian forces occupy Leeuwarden and Groningen

events.enhanced_description: The MV Goya was sunk by the Soviet submarine L-3 in the Baltic Sea while evacuating German troops and civilians as part of Operation Hannibal. The tragedy resulted in the drowning of approximately 7,000 to 8,000 individuals, marking one of the deadliest maritime disasters of the war.
events.name: Sinking of MV Goya

events.enhanced_description: The death marches from Flossenbürg concentration camp began as Nazi forces evacuated prisoners in anticipation of advancing Allied troops. These forced marches led to the suffering and deaths of many inmates, highlighting the brutal conditions of the Holocaust.
events.name: Death marches from Flossenbürg concentration camp begin

events.enhanced_description: Brazilian forces successfully liberated the town of Montese in Italy from German occupation. This operation was part of the broader Allied campaign in Italy, contributing to the eventual defeat of Axis forces in Europe.
events.name: Liberation of Montese, Italy

events.enhanced_description: German occupying forces inundated the Wieringermeer in the Netherlands as part of their defensive strategy during the final stages of World War II. This act was intended to hinder the advancing Allied troops.
events.name: Inundation of Wieringermeer

events.enhanced_description: American troops occupied the German city of Nuremberg, a site previously known for the infamous Nuremberg rallies. This occupation marked a significant step in the Allied efforts to dismantle Nazi power in Germany.
events.name: Occupation of Nuremberg by American troops

events.enhanced_description: Members of the Australian First Tactical Air Force stationed on Morotai in the Dutch East Indies tendered their resignations in protest against being assigned to missions they deemed unimportant. An inquiry later vindicated their actions, highlighting issues of military leadership and morale.
events.name: Morotai Mutiny

events.enhanced_description: Heinrich Himmler, through Count Folke Bernadotte, extended an offer of German surrender to the Western Allies, deliberately excluding the Soviet Union. This maneuver reflected the desperate situation of Nazi leadership as the war was nearing its end.
events.name: Himmler's surrender offer

events.enhanced_description: In a meeting within the Führerbunker, Adolf Hitler acknowledged that 'everything is lost' after learning that SS-Obergruppenführer Felix Steiner could not mobilize enough troops for a counterattack against the encircling Soviet forces. This moment marked a significant turning point in the final days of the Third Reich.
events.name: Hitler concedes everything is lost

events.enhanced_description: Hermann Göring sent a telegram to Adolf Hitler seeking confirmation to assume leadership of Germany, referencing a decree from 1941. Hitler viewed this as an act of treason, further fracturing the already crumbling Nazi leadership.
events.name: Göring telegram to Hitler

events.enhanced_description: The Flossenbürg concentration camp was liberated by the United States Army, revealing the brutal conditions endured by the inmates. This liberation was part of the broader Allied efforts to confront the atrocities committed by the Nazi regime.
events.name: Liberation of Flossenbürg concentration camp

events.enhanced_description: The Red Army completed the encirclement of Berlin, marking a decisive moment in the Battle of Berlin. This encirclement set the stage for the final assault on the German capital, leading to the end of World War II in Europe.
events.name: Battle of Berlin: Red Army encirclement

events.enhanced_description: As they retreated, German troops destroyed all the bridges over the Adige River in Verona, including the historic Ponte di Castelvecchio and Ponte Pietra. This act of destruction was part of their strategy to hinder advancing Allied forces.
events.name: Destruction of bridges in Verona

events.enhanced_description: On Elbe Day, United States and Soviet troops linked up at the Elbe River, effectively cutting Germany in two. This momentous event symbolized the nearing end of World War II in Europe and the division of Germany that would follow.
events.name: Elbe Day: U.S. and Soviet troops link up

events.enhanced_description: Throughout April 1945, numerous significant events occurred during World War II, including battles and military operations across Europe and the Pacific. The month was marked by intense fighting as Allied forces advanced towards Germany and Japan, leading to the eventual conclusion of the war.
events.name: WWII events in April 1945
